Over open country; no damage reported.

Several modular homes were damaged as a brief tornado touched down off of FM 2657, on Sleepy Hollow Lane and Carroll Drive, just inside the Lampasas County line. Homes sustained roof and deck damage and a few were blown slightly off their foundations. Trees and fences were also t…
Tree and minor roof damage was reported. Time estimated.
Quarter-size hail was reported between Lometa and Adamsville.

Quarter-size hail was reported east of Lometa.
Golfball-size hail was reported at the sheriff's office.
A 70 MPH wind gust was measured by amateur radio operators.
Trees were blown over and uprooted and roofs and fences were damaged.
Large limbs were knocked down and trees were uprooted in the city of Lampasas.

A 65 year old large Spanish Oak was uprotted at a home between Lometa and Lampasas. A cedar tree was also twisted on the same property. In the same area, damage at the OJ Ranch consisted of a destroyed barn, a well cover torn off, and several more uprooted large trees.
A highway construction sign was blown across the road and a tree was blown down.

A horse trailer on a property west of Lometa was overturned and tossed through a fence. Several large trees were uprooted at Lometa Regional Park and additional large trees, including cedar trees, were uprooted in and around Lometa. The sign at the Church of Hills was blown out o…
Lots of trees were reported down at and near the intersection of HWY 580 and HWY 581.

A manufactured home on CR 3430 suffered significant damage from straightline winds. Part of the metal roof was peeled back and removed, but the ceiling beams were still in tact. The inside was exposed and damaged by incoming rain.

Hail up to the size of Tennis Balls was reported by a CoCoRaHS observer located 6.2 miles east of Lampasas. The hail lasted for 15 minutes. The hail shredded leaves off trees and tore a few small branches off trees.
Baseball size hail fell along Highway 281 4 miles north of Lampasas.
Baseball size hail fell 3 miles east of Lampasas.
A 60 mph wind gust was estimated 12 miles east of Lampasas.

A 60 foot tall oak tree was uprooted and crashed into a residence on 4th street in Lampasas. The house was significantly damaged. Also in Lampasas, the roof was blown off a portable building at the Lampasas Middle School.
